## GAP_FILL
# Source: the GAP_FILL examples of BigQuery's time series functions
# (third_party/bigquery_docs/reference/standard-sql/time-series-functions.md). Each query reads
# the example's device_data and aggregates the example's result table into one value.

# The locf, linear and null gap-filling methods.
WITH device_data AS (SELECT * FROM UNNEST(ARRAY<STRUCT<device_id INT64, time DATETIME, signal INT64, state STRING>>[STRUCT(1, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:34:01', 74, 'INACTIVE'), STRUCT(2, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:36:00', 77, 'ACTIVE'), STRUCT(3, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:37:00', 78, 'ACTIVE'), STRUCT(4, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:38:01', 80, 'ACTIVE')])) SELECT STRING_AGG(FORMAT('%t=%t', time, signal), ';' ORDER BY time) FROM GAP_FILL(TABLE device_data, ts_column => 'time', bucket_width => INTERVAL 1 MINUTE, value_columns => [('signal', 'locf')])
=> "2023-11-01 09:35:00=74;2023-11-01 09:36:00=77;2023-11-01 09:37:00=78;2023-11-01 09:38:00=78"

WITH device_data AS (SELECT * FROM UNNEST(ARRAY<STRUCT<device_id INT64, time DATETIME, signal INT64, state STRING>>[STRUCT(1, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:34:01', 74, 'INACTIVE'), STRUCT(2, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:36:00', 77, 'ACTIVE'), STRUCT(3, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:37:00', 78, 'ACTIVE'), STRUCT(4, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:38:01', 80, 'ACTIVE')])) SELECT STRING_AGG(FORMAT('%t=%t', time, signal), ';' ORDER BY time) FROM GAP_FILL(TABLE device_data, ts_column => 'time', bucket_width => INTERVAL 1 MINUTE, value_columns => [('signal', 'linear')])
=> "2023-11-01 09:35:00=75;2023-11-01 09:36:00=77;2023-11-01 09:37:00=78;2023-11-01 09:38:00=80"

WITH device_data AS (SELECT * FROM UNNEST(ARRAY<STRUCT<device_id INT64, time DATETIME, signal INT64, state STRING>>[STRUCT(1, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:34:01', 74, 'INACTIVE'), STRUCT(2, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:36:00', 77, 'ACTIVE'), STRUCT(3, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:37:00', 78, 'ACTIVE'), STRUCT(4, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:38:01', 80, 'ACTIVE')])) SELECT STRING_AGG(FORMAT('%t=%t', time, signal), ';' ORDER BY time) FROM GAP_FILL(TABLE device_data, ts_column => 'time', bucket_width => INTERVAL 1 MINUTE, value_columns => [('signal', 'null')])
=> "2023-11-01 09:35:00=NULL;2023-11-01 09:36:00=77;2023-11-01 09:37:00=78;2023-11-01 09:38:00=NULL"

# NULL input values are skipped by default, and kept with ignore_null_values => FALSE.
WITH device_data AS (SELECT * FROM UNNEST(ARRAY<STRUCT<device_id INT64, time DATETIME, signal INT64, state STRING>>[STRUCT(1, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:34:01', 74, 'INACTIVE'), STRUCT(2, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:36:00', 77, 'ACTIVE'), STRUCT(3, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:37:00', NULL, 'ACTIVE'), STRUCT(4, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:38:01', 80, 'ACTIVE')])) SELECT STRING_AGG(FORMAT('%t=%t', time, signal), ';' ORDER BY time) FROM GAP_FILL(TABLE device_data, ts_column => 'time', bucket_width => INTERVAL 1 MINUTE, value_columns => [('signal', 'linear')])
=> "2023-11-01 09:35:00=75;2023-11-01 09:36:00=77;2023-11-01 09:37:00=78;2023-11-01 09:38:00=80"

WITH device_data AS (SELECT * FROM UNNEST(ARRAY<STRUCT<device_id INT64, time DATETIME, signal INT64, state STRING>>[STRUCT(1, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:34:01', 74, 'INACTIVE'), STRUCT(2, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:36:00', 77, 'ACTIVE'), STRUCT(3, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:37:00', NULL, 'ACTIVE'), STRUCT(4, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:38:01', 80, 'ACTIVE')])) SELECT STRING_AGG(FORMAT('%t=%t', time, signal), ';' ORDER BY time) FROM GAP_FILL(TABLE device_data, ts_column => 'time', bucket_width => INTERVAL 1 MINUTE, value_columns => [('signal', 'linear')], ignore_null_values => FALSE)
=> "2023-11-01 09:35:00=75;2023-11-01 09:36:00=77;2023-11-01 09:37:00=NULL;2023-11-01 09:38:00=NULL"

# Without value_columns, every other column is filled with NULL, after the time series column.
WITH device_data AS (SELECT * FROM UNNEST(ARRAY<STRUCT<device_id INT64, time DATETIME, signal INT64, state STRING>>[STRUCT(1, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:34:01', 74, 'INACTIVE'), STRUCT(2, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:36:00', 77, 'ACTIVE'), STRUCT(3, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:37:00', 79, 'ACTIVE'), STRUCT(4, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:38:01', 80, 'ACTIVE')])) SELECT STRING_AGG(TO_JSON_STRING(g), ';' ORDER BY time) FROM GAP_FILL(TABLE device_data, ts_column => 'time', bucket_width => INTERVAL 1 MINUTE) AS g
=> "{\"time\":\"2023-11-01T09:35:00\",\"device_id\":null,\"signal\":null,\"state\":null};{\"time\":\"2023-11-01T09:36:00\",\"device_id\":2,\"signal\":77,\"state\":\"ACTIVE\"};{\"time\":\"2023-11-01T09:37:00\",\"device_id\":3,\"signal\":79,\"state\":\"ACTIVE\"};{\"time\":\"2023-11-01T09:38:00\",\"device_id\":null,\"signal\":null,\"state\":null}"

# Rows of one time point with the same values are condensed.
WITH device_data AS (SELECT * FROM UNNEST(ARRAY<STRUCT<device_id INT64, time DATETIME, signal INT64, state STRING>>[STRUCT(1, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:35:39', 74, 'INACTIVE'), STRUCT(2, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:36:60', 77, 'ACTIVE'), STRUCT(3, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:37:00', 77, 'ACTIVE'), STRUCT(4, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:37:20', 80, 'ACTIVE')])) SELECT STRING_AGG(FORMAT('%t=%t', time, signal), ';' ORDER BY time) FROM GAP_FILL(TABLE device_data, ts_column => 'time', bucket_width => INTERVAL 1 MINUTE, value_columns => [('signal', 'locf')])
=> "2023-11-01 09:36:00=74;2023-11-01 09:37:00=77"

# Each partition is filled separately, between its own first and last time points.
WITH device_data AS (SELECT * FROM UNNEST(ARRAY<STRUCT<device_id INT64, time DATETIME, signal INT64, state STRING>>[STRUCT(2, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:35:07', 87, 'ACTIVE'), STRUCT(1, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:35:26', 82, 'ACTIVE'), STRUCT(3, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:35:39', 74, 'INACTIVE'), STRUCT(2, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:36:07', 88, 'ACTIVE'), STRUCT(1, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:36:26', 82, 'ACTIVE'), STRUCT(2, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:37:07', 88, 'ACTIVE'), STRUCT(1, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:37:28', 80, 'ACTIVE'), STRUCT(3, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:37:39', 77, 'ACTIVE'), STRUCT(2, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:38:07', 86, 'ACTIVE'), STRUCT(1, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:38:26', 81, 'ACTIVE'), STRUCT(3, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:38:39', 77, 'ACTIVE')])) SELECT STRING_AGG(TO_JSON_STRING(g), ';' ORDER BY device_id, time) FROM GAP_FILL(TABLE device_data, ts_column => 'time', bucket_width => INTERVAL 1 MINUTE, partitioning_columns => ['device_id'], value_columns => [('signal', 'locf')]) AS g
=> "{\"time\":\"2023-11-01T09:36:00\",\"device_id\":1,\"signal\":82};{\"time\":\"2023-11-01T09:37:00\",\"device_id\":1,\"signal\":82};{\"time\":\"2023-11-01T09:38:00\",\"device_id\":1,\"signal\":80};{\"time\":\"2023-11-01T09:36:00\",\"device_id\":2,\"signal\":87};{\"time\":\"2023-11-01T09:37:00\",\"device_id\":2,\"signal\":88};{\"time\":\"2023-11-01T09:38:00\",\"device_id\":2,\"signal\":88};{\"time\":\"2023-11-01T09:36:00\",\"device_id\":3,\"signal\":74};{\"time\":\"2023-11-01T09:37:00\",\"device_id\":3,\"signal\":74};{\"time\":\"2023-11-01T09:38:00\",\"device_id\":3,\"signal\":77}"

# Each value column uses its own method.
WITH device_data AS (SELECT * FROM UNNEST(ARRAY<STRUCT<device_id INT64, time DATETIME, signal INT64, state STRING>>[STRUCT(1, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:34:01', 74, 'ACTIVE'), STRUCT(2, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:36:00', 77, 'INACTIVE'), STRUCT(3, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:38:00', 78, 'ACTIVE'), STRUCT(4, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:39:01', 80, 'ACTIVE')])) SELECT STRING_AGG(FORMAT('%t=%t,%t', time, signal, state), ';' ORDER BY time) FROM GAP_FILL(TABLE device_data, ts_column => 'time', bucket_width => INTERVAL 1 MINUTE, value_columns => [('signal', 'linear'), ('state', 'locf')])
=> "2023-11-01 09:35:00=75,ACTIVE;2023-11-01 09:36:00=77,INACTIVE;2023-11-01 09:37:00=78,INACTIVE;2023-11-01 09:38:00=78,ACTIVE;2023-11-01 09:39:00=80,ACTIVE"

# Buckets expand from a custom origin.
WITH device_data AS (SELECT * FROM UNNEST(ARRAY<STRUCT<device_id INT64, time DATETIME, signal INT64, state STRING>>[STRUCT(1, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:34:01', 74, 'ACTIVE'), STRUCT(2, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:36:00', 77, 'INACTIVE'), STRUCT(3, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:38:00', 78, 'ACTIVE'), STRUCT(4, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:39:01', 80, 'ACTIVE')])) SELECT STRING_AGG(FORMAT('%t=%t', time, signal), ';' ORDER BY time) FROM GAP_FILL(TABLE device_data, ts_column => 'time', bucket_width => INTERVAL 1 MINUTE, value_columns => [('signal', 'null')], origin => DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:30:01')
=> "2023-11-01 09:34:01=74;2023-11-01 09:35:01=NULL;2023-11-01 09:36:01=NULL;2023-11-01 09:37:01=NULL;2023-11-01 09:38:01=NULL;2023-11-01 09:39:01=80"

# A subquery is the input.
SELECT STRING_AGG(FORMAT('%t=%t', time, signal), ';' ORDER BY time) FROM GAP_FILL((SELECT * FROM UNNEST(ARRAY<STRUCT<device_id INT64, time DATETIME, signal INT64, state STRING>>[STRUCT(1, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:34:01', 74, 'INACTIVE'), STRUCT(2, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:36:00', 77, 'ACTIVE'), STRUCT(3, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:37:00', 78, 'ACTIVE'), STRUCT(4, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:38:01', 80, 'ACTIVE')])), ts_column => 'time', bucket_width => INTERVAL 1 MINUTE, value_columns => [('signal', 'linear')])
=> "2023-11-01 09:35:00=75;2023-11-01 09:36:00=77;2023-11-01 09:37:00=78;2023-11-01 09:38:00=80"

# Observed BigQuery answers collected with tools/bqanswers.

# The documentation's example of added rows shows 74 at 09:38:00 and 77 at 09:40:00, although
# 09:38:00 has a row of 77 and 09:40:00 a row of 80. BigQuery returns each row's own value at its
# time point, as the documentation's other examples do.
WITH device_data AS (SELECT * FROM UNNEST(ARRAY<STRUCT<device_id INT64, time DATETIME, signal INT64, state STRING>>[STRUCT(1, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:35:39', 74, 'INACTIVE'), STRUCT(2, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:37:39', 77, 'ACTIVE'), STRUCT(3, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:38:00', 77, 'ACTIVE'), STRUCT(4, DATETIME '2023-11-01 09:40:00', 80, 'ACTIVE')])) SELECT STRING_AGG(FORMAT('%t=%t', time, signal), ';' ORDER BY time) FROM GAP_FILL(TABLE device_data, ts_column => 'time', bucket_width => INTERVAL 1 MINUTE, value_columns => [('signal', 'locf')])
=> "2023-11-01 09:36:00=74;2023-11-01 09:37:00=74;2023-11-01 09:38:00=77;2023-11-01 09:39:00=77;2023-11-01 09:40:00=80"

# Rows without a time point are ignored.
SELECT STRING_AGG(FORMAT('%t=%t', t, v), ';' ORDER BY t) FROM GAP_FILL((SELECT DATE '2023-11-01' AS t, 1 AS v UNION ALL SELECT NULL, 2 UNION ALL SELECT DATE '2023-11-03', 3), 't', INTERVAL 1 DAY, value_columns => [('v', 'locf')])
=> "2023-11-01=1;2023-11-02=1;2023-11-03=3"

# FLOAT64 interpolates from the earlier point; INT64 rounds a halfway value toward the later
# point's value.
SELECT STRING_AGG(FORMAT('%t=%t', t, v), ';' ORDER BY t) FROM GAP_FILL((SELECT DATE '2023-11-01' AS t, 1.0 AS v UNION ALL SELECT DATE '2023-11-04', 2.0), 't', INTERVAL 1 DAY, value_columns => [('v', 'linear')])
=> "2023-11-01=1.0;2023-11-02=1.3333333333333333;2023-11-03=1.6666666666666665;2023-11-04=2.0"

SELECT STRING_AGG(FORMAT('%t=%t', t, v), ';' ORDER BY t) FROM GAP_FILL((SELECT DATE '2023-11-01' AS t, -3 AS v UNION ALL SELECT DATE '2023-11-03', -2), 't', INTERVAL 1 DAY, value_columns => [('v', 'linear')])
=> "2023-11-01=-3;2023-11-02=-2;2023-11-03=-2"

SELECT STRING_AGG(FORMAT('%t=%t', t, v), ';' ORDER BY t) FROM GAP_FILL((SELECT DATE '2023-11-01' AS t, 3 AS v UNION ALL SELECT DATE '2023-11-03', 2), 't', INTERVAL 1 DAY, value_columns => [('v', 'linear')])
=> "2023-11-01=3;2023-11-02=2;2023-11-03=2"

SELECT STRING_AGG(FORMAT('%t=%t', t, v), ';' ORDER BY t) FROM GAP_FILL((SELECT DATE '2023-11-01' AS t, -2 AS v UNION ALL SELECT DATE '2023-11-03', -3), 't', INTERVAL 1 DAY, value_columns => [('v', 'linear')])
=> "2023-11-01=-2;2023-11-02=-3;2023-11-03=-3"

# Method names are case-insensitive, and NULL origin, value_columns and partitioning_columns are
# their defaults.
SELECT STRING_AGG(FORMAT('%t=%t', t, v), ';' ORDER BY t) FROM GAP_FILL((SELECT DATE '2023-11-01' AS t, 1 AS v UNION ALL SELECT DATE '2023-11-03', 3), 't', INTERVAL 1 DAY, value_columns => [('v', 'LOCF')])
=> "2023-11-01=1;2023-11-02=1;2023-11-03=3"

SELECT STRING_AGG(FORMAT('%t=%t', t, v), ';' ORDER BY t) FROM GAP_FILL((SELECT DATE '2023-11-01' AS t, 1 AS v UNION ALL SELECT DATE '2023-11-03', 3), 't', INTERVAL 1 DAY, origin => CAST(NULL AS DATE))
=> "2023-11-01=1;2023-11-02=NULL;2023-11-03=3"

SELECT STRING_AGG(FORMAT('%t=%t', t, v), ';' ORDER BY t) FROM GAP_FILL((SELECT DATE '2023-11-01' AS t, 1 AS v UNION ALL SELECT DATE '2023-11-03', 3), 't', INTERVAL 1 DAY, value_columns => NULL)
=> "2023-11-01=1;2023-11-02=NULL;2023-11-03=3"

SELECT STRING_AGG(FORMAT('%t=%t', t, v), ';' ORDER BY t) FROM GAP_FILL((SELECT DATE '2023-11-01' AS t, 1 AS v UNION ALL SELECT DATE '2023-11-03', 3), 't', INTERVAL 1 DAY, partitioning_columns => NULL)
=> "2023-11-01=1;2023-11-02=NULL;2023-11-03=3"

# Buckets of months start at the beginning of a month, or at the origin's day, on the last day of
# a shorter month.
SELECT STRING_AGG(FORMAT('%t', t), ';' ORDER BY t) FROM GAP_FILL((SELECT DATE '2023-01-15' AS t UNION ALL SELECT DATE '2023-04-15'), 't', INTERVAL 1 MONTH)
=> "2023-02-01;2023-03-01;2023-04-01"

SELECT STRING_AGG(FORMAT('%t', t), ';' ORDER BY t) FROM GAP_FILL((SELECT DATETIME '2023-01-15 00:00:00' AS t UNION ALL SELECT DATETIME '2023-04-15 00:00:00'), 't', INTERVAL 1 MONTH)
=> "2023-02-01 00:00:00;2023-03-01 00:00:00;2023-04-01 00:00:00"

SELECT STRING_AGG(FORMAT('%t', t), ';' ORDER BY t) FROM GAP_FILL((SELECT DATE '2023-01-01' AS t UNION ALL SELECT DATE '2023-05-01'), 't', INTERVAL 1 MONTH, origin => DATE '2023-01-15')
=> "2023-01-15;2023-02-15;2023-03-15;2023-04-15"

SELECT STRING_AGG(FORMAT('%t', t), ';' ORDER BY t) FROM GAP_FILL((SELECT DATE '2023-01-01' AS t UNION ALL SELECT DATE '2023-05-01'), 't', INTERVAL 1 MONTH, origin => DATE '2022-12-31')
=> "2023-01-31;2023-02-28;2023-03-31;2023-04-30"
